{{Quote|Know Yourself. Know what you will become!|The Son in before showing [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] the future events of his life and the galaxy|<ref name="Overlords">{{TCW|Overlords}}</ref>}}
The '''Son''', was the incarnation of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] who resided in the [[Planet/Legends|realm]] of [[Mortis/Legends|Mortis]] with [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[The Ones/Legends|family]]&mdash;a dynasty of [[Immortality/Legends|immortal]] [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Celestial/Legends|beings]] who transcended the [[The galaxy/Legends|physical plane of existence]]. Like the other members of his family, the Son was a [[Changeling/Legends|shapeshifter]] who possessed the [[Force power/Legends|power]] to transform into a [[Gargoyle/Legends|winged creature]] that personified his connection to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].

Together with the [[Daughter/Legends|Daughter]], the embodiment of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]], the two siblings shared a mutual enmity for each other and a rivalry that mirrored the two opposing sides of the Force. The Son longed to escape into the galaxy, but his ambitions were hindered by the [[Father (Mortis)/Legends|Father]], who sought to permanently bind his children to Mortis where he could maintain balance between the two. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a [[civil war]] fought between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], the Son saw an opportunity to undermine the Father's rule with the arrival of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], the prophesied [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]]. In his desire to escape Mortis, the Son masterminded a plot to turn Skywalker to the dark side as he believed that only the Chosen One could release him from the confines of Mortis. As a result of the Son's actions, [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] was briefly corrupted but the [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] learner's fall to the dark side failed to turn Skywalker as he and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] refused to harm the young learner. Instead, the Son [[Death/Legends|fatally]] wounded his sister when he attempted to kill the Father with the [[Dagger of Mortis/Legends|Dagger of Mortis]], an unintentional act that he came to regret.

Despite the loss of his sibling, the Son proceeded with his plan to leave Mortis. Through the Son's [[Force vision/Legends|ability]] to see the future, Skywalker foresaw a [[Order 66/Legends|series]] [[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|of]] [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|events]]&mdash;all directly connected to his imminent future, joining forces with the Son in order to end the war. When the Father [[Memory rub/Legends|erased]] the young [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi's]] memories of the visions so that the future would proceed without alteration, the Son, once again denied of the chance to leave Mortis, fought with his father and the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] in a final confrontation. Much to his horror, the Father's suicide robbed the Son of his immortality, allowing the Chosen One to [[Shiak|kill]] the dark one.

==Biography==
===Origin===
{{Quote|Xendor told me he once journeyed to a dead world where the Force was worshiped as a triad of divine beings. The Daughter was the Light Side. The Son was the Dark Side. And the Father? The Father was the Force itself, perhaps.|Arden Lyn, referring to Xendor's description of the Ones|<ref name="TEGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Fanged_God_Book_of_Sith.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Son, an immortal creature of the dark side of the Force.]]
The Son was a physical manifestation of the [[Force power/Legends|power]] of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]<ref name="SWE Son" /> and one of three [[Immortality/Legends|immortal]] [[Celestial/Legends|beings]] known as [[The Ones/Legends|the Ones]]. According to [[Thuruht]] history, the Son and his family lived long before the formation of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]]; they existed over [[100,000 BBY|one hundred thousand]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] [[Galactic Standard Calendar|before]] the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="Apocalypse" /> As the Son was the embodiment of darkness, his only sibling&mdash;the [[Daughter/Legends|Daughter]]&mdash;existed as a counterpart through her status as the incarnation of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]].<ref name="SWE Daughter">{{SWE|characters|daughter|Daughter}}</ref> The patriarch of their dynasty was the [[Father (Mortis)/Legends|Father]], a [[Unifying Force/Legends|unifying figure]] dedicated to the preservation of balance between the two opposing aspects of the Force&mdash;and by extension, the rivalry between his children.<ref name="SWE Father">{{SWE|characters|father|Father}}</ref> As a member of the Ones, the Son possessed a unique [[Changeling/Legends|shapeshifting ability]] that enabled him to transform into a [[Gargoyle/Legends|winged creature]] that personified his personal connection to the Force.<ref name="Overlords" />

The Thuruht held that the history of the Ones, revealed to them through revelations from both the Son and the Daughter, began with the trio's residence on a [[Abeloth's planet|jungle-covered]] [[Planet/Legends|world]], located in [[Maw Cluster/Legends|the Maw]] section of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], where they lived together in peace and harmony. However, the tranquility of their realm was destroyed when the Son, in defiance of the Father, drank from the [[Font of Power]], an act that corrupted his nature and recreated him as the essence of the dark side. The fall of the Son was swiftly followed by the Daughter's rebirth as the quintessence of the light side, the result of her bathing in the [[Pool of Knowledge]], also in defiance of the Father's will. As with the light and the darkness, the two siblings developed a rivalry and competed against one another for dominance, causing them both to divide the planet between their respective dominions. Horrified by his family's descent into discord, the Father became the balance of the Force itself through his attempts to curb the growing conflict between his wayward offspring.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

[[File:SiblingSmackdown-AOM.png|thumb|right|250px|The Daughter and the Son, symbolizing the battle between light and darkness respectively.]]
The remedy to the strife within the Ones presented itself in the person of [[Abeloth]], the Bringer of Chaos and originally a young woman who catered to the needs of the Ones through her role as the Servant. It was not long until she became an honorary member of the Ones through her new role as the Mother. In addition to her close relationship with the Father, the Mother successfully reconciled the siblings and influenced them in restoring their world to its former glory. Under the Mother's guidance, the Son channeled his destructive energies through a constructive approach by carving out caves and passages in the walls of their valley. But despite the many years that marked the family's reconciliation, the Mother's mortality remained in effect and she continued to age while her family remained ageless. Hampered by extreme old age, she could no longer suppress the natural instincts of the Son and the Daughter. Thus, the period of restored happiness was ended by the renewed conflict between brother and sister.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

The Mother, fearful that the Ones would abandon her, sought to prevent her own death by attaining eternal life. With the Father distracted by the fighting between his children, the Mother drank from the Font of Power and bathed in the Pool of Knowledge, both of which were strictly forbidden by the Father. Through the two power sources, the Mother&mdash;now reborn as Abeloth&mdash;became a more powerful Force wielder than the Son and the Daughter. In light of the threat that Abeloth posed to the Ones, the Son formed an alliance with his sister and father in their combined efforts to contain Abeloth on their former homeworld. As a result, they were also forced to leave the planet as well, stranding Abeloth in the process while searching for a new home.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

Knowing that their one-time matriarch posed a threat to both their interests, the Son and his sister temporarily suspended their rivalry in order to prevent Abeloth from escaping the confines of her [[Prison/Legends|prison]]. Locating the Thuruht, a [[Killik/Legends|Killik]] [[Species/Legends|race]] from [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], the Ones [[Joiner|joined]] the hivemind through the Force. Using the Thuruht as a workforce, the Ones influenced the construction of [[Centerpoint Station]], [[Sinkhole Station]] and several other technological wonders, all designed to strengthen the containment of Abeloth. Following the completion of their creations, the Son retreated with his family to Mortis,<ref name="Apocalypse" /> a realm that transcended the confines of the physical universe<ref name="SWE Mortis">{{SWE|locations|mortis|Mortis}}</ref> where they remained for many millennia, emerging only to defeat Abeloth whenever she escaped from her prison world.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

[[File:MortisSurface.png|thumb|left|250px|Mortis, home to the Father and the Daughter, but a prison to the Son.]]
By [[24,500 BBY]], during the early period of the Ancient Republic, the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|fallen]] [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Xendor]] discovered Mortis where he encountered the Ones. Through his interactions with the immortal beings, he gathered that they each embodied a certain aspect of the Force&mdash;the Daughter personified the light; the Son was darkness incarnate; and the Father was essentially the balance that existed between the Force's two warring sides. Though he later relayed his discovery of the Ones to [[Arden Lyn]], another former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], Xendor remained firmly committed to the belief system of the [[Legions of Lettow]], a heretical splinter group of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], and dismissed the Ones' claims as no more legitimate than the other theories regarding the nature of the Force.<ref name="TEGTW" />

===Arrival of the Chosen One===
{{Quote|It's true, what they say. You ''are'' the Chosen One.|The Son, to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Altar">{{TCW|Altar of Mortis (episode)}}</ref>}}
[[File:SonRevealed.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Son introduces himself to Tano and Kenobi.]]
Although the Father had preserved the balance between the light and dark sides of the Force&mdash;in the persons of his offspring&mdash;for hundreds of thousands of years, his immortality had begun to fail him, convincing the Father that his own [[Death/Legends|death]] was imminent. Around the same time, the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] was being waged between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the breakaway [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. In the midst of the [[civil war]], the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] fought on the side of the Republic and was believed by some within the Jedi Order to be the legendary [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]]; a Jedi, born through the Force, destined to restore balance between the light and the darkness. The Father, desperate for a successor, planted an ancient Jedi [[Distress signal/Legends|distress signal]] in the [[Chrelythiumn system/Legends|Chrelythiumn system]] that drew Skywalker, [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], and [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] to the Mortis realm via a [[Mortis monolith/Legends|monolith-like gateway]].<ref name="Overlords" />

While the Daughter remained loyal and subservient to the Father, the Son became intrigued by how the Chosen One's arrival presented him with a long-awaited opportunity to escape the confines of Mortis. As the Daughter led the three Jedi to the Father's [[Mortis monastery/Legends|monastery]], the Son caused a large rock to collapse on a cliff path, dividing Kenobi and Tano from Skywalker. When the two Jedi returned to the landing site of their [[Eta-class shuttle/Legends|Eta-class shuttle]], the Son briefly confronted them and eagerly inquired about whether or not Skywalker truly was the Chosen One. Kenobi and Tano ignited their lightsabers, asking him how he knew about the Prophecy. The Son simply said they couldn't do anything to stop the future from happening, simultaneously deactivating their lightsabers with a wave of his wand. Kenobi called him a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. Son laughed at the notion, which he then confirmed and denied&mdash;he embodied the source of the [[Order of the Sith Lords|Sith's]] power, but was not actual member. Before leaving them, he warned them that the storms were lethal and they should find shelter.<ref name="Overlords" />

Soon afterward, the Son indirectly confronted Skywalker through an apparition of the young Jedi Knight's deceased [[Parent/Legends|mother]] [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker Lars]]. The spectrum of his mother compelled Skywalker to admit his failings as a son and a Jedi; the guilt he harbored over the [[Mission to rescue Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|massacre]] of the [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]]; and his fear of loss regarding [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], the woman with whom he secretly entered a [[Jedi Code/Legends|forbidden]] [[Marriage/Legends|marriage]] with. At this, his mother's appearance transformed into the visage of the Son's winged beast form and declared that Amidala was only a distraction that obstructed the Chosen One from the fulfillment of his destiny.<ref name="Overlords" />

[[File:KneelBeforeZod-Overlords.png|thumb|left|250px|The Daughter and the Son, brought to heel by the power of the Chosen One.]]
In order to determine if Skywalker truly was the Chosen One, the Father created a scenario in which the young Jedi Knight would be forced to demonstrate his powers. To this end, the Son abducted Ahsoka Tano while the Daughter captured Obi-Wan Kenobi. Both were brought to the monastery where the Father challenged Skywalker to choose which one was to be spared. Although he was torn by indecision and conflicted by the knowledge that either choice sentenced the other to death, Skywalker used his fear and desperation as amplifiers for his powers. Through the Force, he [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetically]] freed Kenobi and Tano before forcing the Son and the Daughter to their knees in submission. The show of power was enough to convince the Ones that he was in fact the Chosen One, but Skywalker refused to remain on Mortis as the Father's successor. He instead returned with his former Master and Padawan to their [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] and attempted to leave the Father and his children behind on Mortis.<ref name="Overlords" />

===The Son's machinations===
{{Quote|I have done what is right or what is wrong, depending on your point of view.|The Son, referring to his actions and the subjective status of terms such as right and wrong|<ref name="Altar" />}}
[[File:SonGargoyle-AOM.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Son captures Tano.]]
As the Jedi trio attempted to depart from Mortis, the Son devised a strategy to enter the physical plane of existence, primarily through the Chosen One whom he intended to corrupt with the power of the dark side of the Force. Approaching Anakin Skywalker in a dream, the Son took the Chosen One's form and offered to form an alliance with him, with their objective being peace and stability throughout the universe. When Skywalker refused to submit to the dark side on the grounds that he would never join the Sith, the Son's original form became enraged and claimed that they would destroy the Sith and Jedi alike. Shortly after Skywalker awoke from the dream, the Son boarded the shuttle and abducted Ahsoka Tano, intending to use her as a catalyst for Skywalker's fall to the dark side.<ref name="Altar" />

After imprisoning Tano within his [[Son's cathedral/Legends|tower]], the Son&mdash;disguised as a seemingly harmless creature&mdash;confronted the Padawan over her inner fears and doubts. However, Tano refused to give in to her anger and remained convinced that her Master would come to her aid. Seeing that she would not turn on her own volition, the creature bit Tano's arm, infecting her with the dark side so that she would become completely subservient to the Son. With Tano firmly placed under his control, the Son deployed the Padawan to the tower's courtyard where she awaited Skywalker's arrival. When Tano showed him her confidence, the Son infected the Padawan and clouded her mind with the Dark Side. No longer restrained by her [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi upbringing]], Tano became consumed with a hatred over her insecurities and low self-esteem, all of which had been developed through her fear that she was never fit to be the apprentice of the Chosen One.<ref name="Altar" />

[[File:SonPoisonsAhsoka-AOM.png|thumb|left|250px|The Son turns Tano to the dark side of the Force.]]
Following his capture of Tano, the Son traveled to the monastery where he consulted with the Father during the Daughter's [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]]. The Father accused his son of interfering with the will of the Force and also sensed his deeper immersion within the dark side. The Son dismissed the Father's lecture and asserted that while his power continued to grow, the Father became older and even more frail. In response, the Father threatened that the Son would be contained through force if he did not disengage from his plans to leave Mortis. The Son, no longer willing to tolerate the Father's control over his life, attacked him with [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] and proclaimed his absolute hatred for the being who had long since hindered his desire for freedom. Transforming into his beast form, the Son returned to his tower where he anticipated the imminent battle between Skywalker and his fallen apprentice.<ref name="Altar" />

The Son reveled in Tano's fury, sensing the rage and frustration that she had suppressed and kept hidden from her Master. While Skywalker and Tano [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|dueled]] in the courtyard, the Daughter and Obi-Wan Kenobi confronted the Son in his throne room, shortly after they had retrieved the [[Dagger of Mortis/Legends|Dagger of Mortis]], the only weapon that possessed the power to either control or kill the Ones. However, Kenobi was forced to help Skywalker against the corrupted Padawan learner, leaving the Daughter to stand against her brother alone. Beseeching him to abandon the dark side, the Daughter's efforts were rebuffed by the Son who refused to allow her to interfere with his plans. The two proved evenly matched against one another; neither could gain the decisive advantage despite the Son's mastery of Force lightning or the Daughter's proficiency in telekinesis. They remained deadlocked in a stalemate even in their beast forms, until the recovered Father arrived and forced them out into the courtyard. Declaring the Father to be weak and irrelevant, the Son retaliated with a Force lightning attack to which the Father attempted to [[Tutaminis|absorb]] and deflect. His power diminished, the Father's control over the Son was broken, causing him to fall in defeat as the Son increased his lightning attack in its intensity.<ref name="Altar" />

[[File:TheOnesDaughterDeath-AOM.png|thumb|right|250px|The Son accidentally kills the Daughter.]]
With the Son distracted by his attack on the Father, Kenobi and Skywalker intended to kill him by using the Dagger of Mortis, but were prevented from doing so when Tano stole the weapon and presented it to the Son. Reveling in his apparent triumph, the Son tapped Tano on the forehead, causing her to fall into a near-death state. With the Father at his mercy, the Son raised the dagger to kill him, but unintentionally stabbed his sister in the back as she moved to shield their father from the blade with her own body. The Son was shocked by what had transpired.<ref name="Altar" /> In spite of his existence as the incarnated form of the dark side, he still loved the Daughter.<ref name="SWE Son" /> Enraged over the setback, the Son shifted back into a gargoyle and flew away from the tower. As her last act before dying, the Daughter successfully aided Skywalker in his attempt to save Tano from death.<ref name="Altar" />

===The future revealed===
{{Quote|Join me, and together we will destroy this Emperor you see in your visions. Then, we shall end war, corruption, and suffering throughout the galaxy.|The Son and Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Ghosts">{{TCW|Ghosts of Mortis}}</ref>}}
[[File:AnakinSeduced-GOM.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Son offers Skywalker a chance to see the future.]]
Unconvinced that the Father was able to contain the Son by himself, Anakin Skywalker followed the instructions of a [[Force ghost/Legends|ghostly apparition]] of [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and journeyed to the [[Well of the Dark Side/Legends|Well of the Dark Side]] where he was confronted by the Son. Not wishing to fight, the Son offered to share his knowledge of the future with Skywalker. The initial [[Force vision/Legends|visions]] that he shared frightened and confused Skywalker, but the Jedi Knight's attempts to resist the visions, in which he saw the outcome of the war and his own dark destiny, proved futile.<ref name="Ghosts" />

The Son, stripping the future away, allowed the Chosen One to see himself as [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious's]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]],<ref name="Ghosts" /><ref name="SWE Sidious">{{SWE|characters|darthsidious|Darth Sidious}}</ref> [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|hunting down]] and [[Order 66/Legends|murdering]] members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] (including child [[Initiate/Legends|Initiates]] during the [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|siege]] of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]]), choking Padmé Amidala with his own hands, his [[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|defeat in battle]] against Obi-Wan Kenobi,<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] via the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|original Death Star]],<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> and ultimately his future as a broken [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] reconstructed with extensive [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic replacements]] and a [[Breath mask/Legends|pressurized]] [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|suit of armor]].

[[File:AnakinVaderVision-GOM.png|thumb|right|250px|With the Son's help, Skywalker foresees his future.]]
The Son's tactic succeeded in rendering Skywalker emotionally vulnerable and far more susceptible to the allure of the dark side. Now aware of Sidious's imminent [[Declaration of a New Order|rise]] as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] in a [[Imperial Era/Legends|period]] of wide-spread suffering and destruction, Skywalker agreed to bring the Son to the galaxy so that together they might prevent the very future Skywalker beheld in vision. Believing that the Jedi Order would obstruct his ability to change the course of history, Skywalker renounced his ties to the Jedi and willingly embraced the Son's power and promise.<ref name="Ghosts" />

===Death===
{{Quote|And so you have betrayed me, Father.|The Son's last words before death|<ref name="Ghosts" />}}
[[File:SonsDeath-GhostsOfMortis.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Chosen One kills the Son.]]
Obi-Wan Kenobi, rushing to the Well of the Dark Side to aid Skywalker against the temptations and power of the Son, discovered, however, that his former apprentice had already made his choice and turned to the dark side. Using Kenobi's distraction to his advantage, the Son attacked the Jedi Master with Force lightning before disappearing. The two Jedi, having resisted the Son's attack, made their way to the shuttle. Even so, their efforts to return to the known galaxy had been obstructed by Ahsoka Tano. Leaving the shuttle's control system sabotaged, Ahsoka retreated to the monastery, but was followed there by her Master and Obi-Wan.<ref name="Ghosts" />

By the [[Time/Legends|time]] the Son arrived, it became clear to him that escape would be impossible as long as the Father continued to live. The Son had instructed Skywalker to remain with the shuttle while he searched for the Father, unaware that the Father was using the diversion as an opportunity to [[Memory rub/Legends|erase]] the Chosen One's memories of his dark visions, to ensure that the future would unfold naturally, unmarred by the Son's interference.<ref name="Ghosts" />

Now finding the Father, along with Skywalker, Kenobi and Tano at the monastery, and ignoring the Father's final plea to abandon the dark side, the Son fought and overpowered all three Jedi with ease. In order to bring an end to the conflict and the Son's schemes, the Father took the Dagger of Mortis from him and stabbed himself through the chest. Much to the Son's surprise, his own connection to the Force was tied to the life of the Father. With the Father fatally wounded, the Son lost his powers and immortality, allowing Skywalker to [[Shiak|strike]] down the now mortal Son with [[Anakin Skywalker's second lightsaber/Legends|his lightsaber]]. With his last breath, the Son accused the Father of treachery before succumbing to death.<ref name="Ghosts" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|And now I die, my heart broken, knowing the role you will play.|The Father's dying words, hinting to Anakin Skywalker about his future as Darth Vader|<ref name="Ghosts" />}}
Upon the Jedi trio's return to the galaxy, an [[Mission to Mortis/Legends|official report]] was filed on the encounter with the Ones on Mortis&mdash;one that remained dormant within the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]] for decades, until it was rediscovered in [[44 ABY]] by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], the son of the Chosen One and the [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] of the [[New Jedi Order]]. Through the report, augmented by information from the Thuruht hivemind, Skywalker came to believe that his father's refusal to remain on Mortis (and thereby restore balance) caused a chain of events that hurled the galaxy into an unprecedented period of chaos and disorder, primarily through the disruptive events that followed the Clone Wars and the birth of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], such as the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[Swarm War]] and the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]&mdash;all of which occurred on a galactic scale in less than a hundred years' time.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

Anakin Skywalker's legacy with regard to the Ones of Mortis touched also his direct descendant, Sith Lord [[Darth Caedus]]. As a result of Caedus's actions, Centerpoint Station was inadvertently [[Battle of Centerpoint Station (Second Galactic Civil War)|destroyed]], allowing Abeloth to escape into the galaxy without interference from the Ones. In light of the threat that Abeloth posed to the Jedi and the Sith, both Orders effectively replaced the Daughter and the Son in their capacity to hold Abeloth at bay, culminating in the defeat of the Bringer of Chaos during her battle with Luke Skywalker and [[Darth Krayt]] of the [[One Sith]].<ref name="Apocalypse" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Do not hate him, Father. It is his nature.|The Daughter, referring to the Son and the dark side as one and the same|<ref name="Altar" />}}
[[File:SonInDream-AOM.png|thumb|right|250px|The Son, displaying his anger and desire for the destruction of Sith and Jedi alike.]]
The Son was the personification of the power of the dark side.<ref name="SWE Son" /> From the [[Daughter/Legends|Daughter's]] point of view, her brother could not be anything other than manipulative, deceitful, resentful and homicidal because his personality was a reflection of the nature of the dark side of the Force.<ref name="Altar" /> Throughout the centuries, the Son was grudgingly subservient to the Father's will, but a lack of independence caused him to resent the control that the Father exerted over his life.<ref name="SWE Son" /> Longing to be free with the full power of the dark side at his command, the Son was initially content to bide his time until the Father's immortality faded, leaving the latter powerless to further restrain the Son.<ref name="Altar" /> The only times he would willingly work with his Father was when fighting [[Abeloth]].

Regardless of the Son's affiliation with the dark side, he remained emotionally attached to the Daughter,<ref name="SWE Son" /> the only one he ever loved.<ref name="Ghosts" /> However, in spite of the Son's affinity for his sister, the Daughter was also a source of her brother's hatred due to her status as the embodiment of the light side. He did not hesitate to attack her whenever he felt provoked into doing so. Nevertheless, her unexpected death at his hands deeply affected the Son,<ref name="Altar" /> causing him to mourn the loss of his sister in secret.<ref name="Ghosts" />

Aside from his anger and lust for power, the Son showed himself to be a patient and calculating individual, as well as a meticulous schemer who sought to utilize every advantage at his disposal. By abducting [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] and stating his intentions to leave [[Mortis/Legends|Mortis]], the Son baited his enemies into a trap that was designed to bring him the [[Dagger of Mortis/Legends|Dagger of Mortis]] and the Father in one place; the only setback in his plan was the Daughter's interference in the Son's attempt at committing patricide. He was also subjected to occasional fits of rage and impetuousness whenever he encountered obstacles to his ambitions, such as when [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] initially refused to join him and when the Father made clear that the Son would never be allowed to enter the physical universe.<ref name="Altar" />

Much like Darth Sidious, the Son saw himself and the dark side as the natural remedy to a galaxy that was falling increasingly into a state of anarchy and chaos. He firmly believed that the power of the dark side was capable of forging a new and everlasting era of order and tranquility that he and the Chosen One could establish a balance throughout the universe, but only through full submission to the dark side.<ref name="Altar" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Can you feel it, Sister? Can you feel the anger? The hate? The fury?''"<br />"''Their conflict is feeding you, isn't it?|The Son, and the Daughter|<ref name="Altar" />}}
[[File:Epguide316.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Son casts Force lightning.]]
While the Son's powers were directly from the dark side of the Force, much like the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] themselves, his [[Force-sensitive/Legends|connection]] to the Force existed on a level beyond the domain of most Sith.<ref name="SWE Son" /> Given his existence as a manifestation of the dark side,<ref name="TEGTW" /> and combined with experience that stretched over eons of time,<ref name="Apocalypse" /> the Son's proficiency with the power of the dark side was great, even threatening his family members.<ref name="Overlords" /><ref name="Altar" /><ref name="Ghosts" /> The Son was highly skilled in Force lightning which he held as his primary form of attack; unlike most wielders, the Son's Force lightning was red. He also proved himself to be a skilled practitioner in several variations of telekinesis and could [[Floating Meditation|float]] down and up a valley. He also could [[Injure/Kill|take life with a touch]].<ref name="Altar" /><ref name="Ghosts" />

An almost immortal being, the Son was a highly skilled combatant and only a handful of individuals, such as the Father, the Daughter, Abeloth,<ref name="Apocalypse" /> and Anakin Skywalker were known to have faced him with success in battle.<ref name="Altar" /> Moreover, Obi-Wan survived being attacked by his lightning bolts.<ref name="Ghosts" /> Like the rest of the Ones, the Son wielded the ability to [[Metamorphosis|transform]] his appearance into virtually anything he wanted. Aside from his primary [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] form, the Son favored the appearance of a large, winged gargoyle which he utilized for purposes of combat and travel. He also could [[Fold space|move from place to place in an instant]] and took on the forms of [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker]],<ref name="Overlords" /> Anakin Skywalker, and a diminutive creature during the Jedi's stay on Mortis. Allegedly he was able to [[Consume Essence|grow stronger via the dark deeds of others]].<ref name="Altar" />

His ability to use the offensive applications of the dark side notwithstanding, the Son was also able to channel the Force in less combative ways. The range of his more passive uses of power included his self-manifestation within one of Skywalker's dreams, the ability to appear and disappear at will without alerting others to his presence and a unique capacity to literally infect an individual with the dark side's influence&mdash;a power which gave him an [[Qâzoi Kyantuska|enhanced measure of control]] over Ahsoka Tano's mind.<ref name="Altar" />

In the Son's form as the Fanged God, per Nightsister tradition he was rumored to be so powerful that (allegedly) channeling his power could burst minor blood vessels in the physical bodies of his followers and pawns, raising telltale bruises on their cheeks and around their eyes, though in fact these techniques remained both useable and possibly harmful to the user after his death.<ref name="WP" /><ref name="The Courtship of Princess Leia">''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]''</ref> It was also said that he was the one who conjured up the Wild Hunt each year on [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] for the Nightsisters. It was said that he could also seep through the borders that separated his realm from the physical realm though it does not take much of his effort to do so.<ref name="WP">''[[Wild Power]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Son first appeared in the [[Mortis/Legends|Mortis]] story arc of the [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]] in the television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''. The Son was voiced by [[Sam Witwer]], who previously voiced [[Galen Marek]] in ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed|The Force Unleashed]]'' and would go on to voice [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]]. The Son was also voiced by [[Pernilla August]] (while masquerading as Shmi Skywalker), [[Matt Lanter]] (while masquerading as Anakin Skywalker) and [[Ashley Eckstein]] (while possessing Ahsoka Tano).
